lastText: The Campaign EndsThe ReckoningNew Ending Found · 1 / 16CONFESSION NAMES SECOND PARTY; PATRON’S IDENTITY STILL UNKNOWNThe full ledger reaches the Rector’s desk on a Tuesday, in Victor’s own hand, and this time it names names, including a benefactor Victor himself met only once, through Fritz, and never saw again. The inquest that follows spends as much time chasing that unnamed patron as it does Victor, and never quite catches either. He is not thanked for the confession. He is not forgiven for it. But for the first time in a year, the debt is not his alone to carry, and Fritz, when they finally speak of it, will say only that he did what the money asked and hoped it would be enough. The legend that survives is a careful, complicated one. Those who claim to have spoken with it describe something neither quite a monster nor quite a man: measured, watchful, and difficult to read. It seems to want something from the world it was given.
